# Chicago Rental Issue: Mold, Leak, and Tenant Protection Plan

You can treat this as a repair-and-documentation issue first: notify the landlord in writing, request prompt repairs, and keep a clean paper trail in case the problem escalates. The goal is to be polite, specific, and consistent.

# Practical Tenant Checklist and Repair Request

| Step | What to Do | Why It Helps |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Take dated photos and short videos of the mold, wall damage, and leaking sink | Creates proof of the condition and severity |
| 2 | Write down when you first noticed each issue and whether it is getting worse | Shows timeline and urgency |
| 3 | Send the landlord a written notice by email and, if possible, certified mail | Gives you a clear record that they were informed |
| 4 | Ask for repair dates and keep all replies | Confirms the request and any promises made |
| 5 | Avoid discussing the issue only by phone or text | Written communication is easier to document |
| 6 | Keep paying rent on time unless you receive advice from a qualified local attorney or tenant group | Helps reduce retaliation risk |
| 7 | Save receipts for any temporary cleanup or damage-prevention steps | Supports reimbursement or later claims |
| 8 | If the problem worsens or affects habitability, contact a local tenant-rights group or city housing help line | Helps you understand next steps without guessing |

## Polite Repair Request Message

Subject: Repair Request — Mold in Bathroom Wall and Leaking Sink

Hello [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I’m writing to notify you of two maintenance issues in my apartment at [address/unit]:

- Mold is visible on one bathroom wall.
- The bathroom sink is leaking.

The lease term is 2025-09-01 through 2026-08-31, and I want to make sure the apartment is kept in a safe and livable condition. Please arrange for an inspection and repairs as soon as possible.

I would appreciate a written response with:
- A date for inspection
- A repair timeline
- The name of the person or company handling the work

I have photos and notes documenting the issues and can provide them if helpful. Please let me know the next steps.

Thank you for your prompt attention.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Apartment number]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

## Record-Keeping Plan

- Create one folder for this issue with subfolders for photos, videos, emails, letters, and receipts.
- Save each photo/video with the date in the filename, such as `2025-05-19_bathroom_mold.jpg`.
- Keep a simple log with these entries:
  - Date noticed
  - What happened
  - Who you told
  - How you contacted them
  - Their response
- Screenshot any texts or portal messages and keep the full conversation thread.
- Save copies of your lease, move-in inspection report, and any prior maintenance requests.
- After every landlord reply, send a short follow-up email summarizing what was said so there is a written record.
- If someone enters to inspect or repair, note the date, time, name, and what work was done.
- If you notice retaliation concerns, document the change immediately with dates and facts only.
